It is one of the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|ja|伊豆国の式内社一覧|qid=Q11380552|lt=Shikinai shrines of Izu Province}}<ref name="yuisho">Shrine grounds historical notice</ref>.

=== Overview ===
The date of foundation is unknown, but as it is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai shrine}}, it dates back to before {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}, the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}}, when the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' was compiled<ref>[https://kotobank.jp/word/神名帳-82644 What is the Jinmyōchō] - {{ill|Kotobank|Q11302260|qid=Q11302260}}</ref>.

From ancient times it was called Ugusu Daimyōjin / Mishima Daimyōjin and was revered as a deity of agriculture, fishing, and commerce, but in September {{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 7) it was renamed Ugusu Shrine<ref name="yuisho"/>.

In {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} (Reiwa 4), an event called “Wind Chime Shrine” was held, in which 240 wind chimes were decorated in the worship hall, hosted by Nishiizu Glass Studio<ref>[https://ikoyo-nishiizu.jp/glass/fuurinjinnjya.pdf Wind Chime Shrine] - Ikōyo Nishiizu</ref><ref>[https://ikoyo-nishiizu.jp/glass/ Nishiizu Glass Studio] - Ikōyo Nishiizu</ref>.

=== Cultural properties ===
* Main hall - Constructed in March {{ill|1598|Q6800|qid=Q6800}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 3)<ref name="yuisho"/>.
* Hanging {{ill|Stone lantern|Q12012294|qid=Q12012294}} - Dedicated in November {{ill|1609|Q6762|qid=Q6762}} (Keichō 14) by {{ill|Ōkubo Nagayasu|Q133746|qid=Q133746}}<ref name="yuisho"/>. Designated Tangible Cultural Property of the prefecture<ref name="yuisho"/><ref>[https://www.town.nishiizu.shizuoka.jp/kakuka/kankou/kankou/meisyo/youmeiji.html Ugusu Shrine] - Nishiizu Town</ref><ref>[https://www.nishiizu-kankou.com/sightseeing/ugusujinjya Ugusu Shrine] - Nishiizu Town Tourism Association</ref><ref>[https://www.pref.shizuoka.jp/kankosports/bunkageijutsu/bunkazai/1002825/1041003/1041888/1004974/1021024.html Shizuoka Cultural Property Navi: Hanging Lantern] - Shizuoka Prefecture</ref>.
* {{ill|Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry|Q671039|qid=Q671039}} paintings - Donated in August {{ill|1612|Q6771|qid=Q6771}} (Keichō 17) by Hattori Daizō and two others<ref name="yuisho"/>.
